purpose: Define authored/canonical runtime definitions as inert semantics distinct from mutable runtime state created while the system is operating.

owns: Runtime Definition and State Separation semantics

topics.name: Definition vs State
topics.purpose: Define authored/canonical runtime definitions as inert semantics distinct from mutable runtime state created while the system is operating.

semantics.definition: Stable declarative semantics/metadata loaded from authoritative sources.
semantics.runtime_state: Mutable operational state produced while resolving/executing definitions.
semantics.separation_rule: Runtime state changes do not silently rewrite authoritative definitions.
semantics.timing_state_rule: Trigger timing, inflight gates, queue state, runner lifecycle and similar operational state belong to runtime state unless explicitly defined otherwise.
semantics.reload_rule: Reload of definitions reconciles source-owned definition state without silently destroying unrelated runtime-owned state.
semantics.persistence_rule: Persistence of runtime state requires an explicit owning contract; persistence is not implied by existence.

invariants.rule: Runtime-significant semantics are explicit and do not arise from payload, path, projection or implementation heuristics.

hard_gates.condition: runtime mutation silently rewrites authoritative definition
ephemeral timing/gate/queue state stored as definition semantics
definition read causes runtime state mutation
reload destroys unrelated runtime-owned state without explicit lifecycle rule
runtime state becomes persistent canonical semantics merely because it exists

references.purpose: Runtime state changes are not canonical writes.
